title: Console observability MVP: scope reductions and acceptance criteria for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Aisha Brennan
description: Context: We need to ship a first-pass Redwood Console observability surface that delivers immediate value for product and platform teams without blocking the Dedicated/private rollout timeline or incurring major infra risk. This ticket documents deliberate MVP cuts across three areas (dashboards, tracing, cost breakdown), the rationale, and acceptance criteria for the trimmed scope. The goal is to ship incremental visibility that drives troubleshooting and cost optimization while keeping implementation size and SLO risk bounded.
background: User research and early customer requests prioritized: (1) quick identification of high-latency routes, (2) basic request-level tracing to investigate outliers, and (3) top-line cost drivers per model/route. Original scope included advanced features (full trace waterfall UI, per-token cost attribution across layers, customizable dashboard widgets). Those features introduce backend indexing, heavy storage, and UI complexity that would push the release by 6+ weeks.
scope_changes_summary: MVP cuts applied to meet release window: 1) Dashboards: ship a curated set of three pre-built dashboards (Traffic, Latency, Errors) limited to 30-day time range and no widget editor. 2) Tracing: implement sampled traces at 1% baseline with ability to increase sample rate via feature flag; show collapsed span summary with top 3 expensive spans, no live waterfall or span-level flame graph. 3) Cost breakdown: present aggregated daily cost per model and top-10 routes by spend; defer per-token component breakdown and continuous attribution to a follow-up. Additionally, remove per-token client-side attribution visualization from MVP.
out_of_scope:
- Full trace waterfall + flame graph UI
- Per-token cost slice (tokenization vs model vs I/O)
- Dashboard widget authoring and saved filters beyond global time range
- Long-term cold storage for raw traces (only sampled traces stored for 7d in MVP)
- Advanced rollups for multi-region cost attribution
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: Three pre-built dashboards available (Traffic, Latency, Errors) accessible from Console nav
Dashboards: Default 7-day and optional 30-day ranges supported; initial load for default range loads under 1.0s for 95th percentile requests in staging with realistic dataset
Dashboards: Each dashboard contains at least 4 read-only widgets (time series, heatmap, topN table, failure rate) populated from existing metrics pipeline
Tracing: Traces UI shows sampled traces (1% baseline) with summary header, latency timeline, and collapsed span list showing top 3 spans by duration
Tracing: Selecting a trace displays raw event list and request metadata (route, model, tenant) but not full span flame graphs
Cost breakdown: UI shows daily aggregated spend per model and top 10 routes by spend for a selectable 7/30-day range
Cost breakdown: Cost numbers align with billing view within 3% for sample customers and are queryable via Console API for export
Rollout: Feature flag gating implemented for trace sampling configuration and cost breakdown visibility; staged rollout to 10% of orgs then 100%
Telemetry: Console emits telemetry events for view_open, widget_refresh, trace_view, and cost_export; events must include tenant_id and model_id
Security: Sampled traces redact user prompt content and any <PII> tokens before storage; reviewed by Security and approved
Tests: End-to-end tests for dashboard load, trace view, and cost export exist in CI and pass on release branch
decisions: Ship curated read-only dashboards instead of dashboard builder to reduce UI surface and accelerate delivery
Implement trace sampling and minimal trace UI instead of full waterfall to avoid heavy storage and indexing costs
Show aggregated cost/top routes, defer per-token component cost breakdown to next cycle
Gate sampling rate and cost UI behind feature flags for controlled rollout and rapid rollback if infra impacts observed
tradeoffs: Speed-to-market vs completeness: Cutting per-token breakdown reduces immediate ability to attribute costs to tokenization/I/O, but enables earlier customer value (top spenders by route/model)
Operational cost vs fidelity: Sampling reduces storage and query cost but may miss infrequent performance regressions; mitigated by ability to temporarily bump sample rate per org
Developer velocity vs future rework: Read-only dashboards reduce front-end work but may require later rework when adding widget editor and saved filters
engineering_notes: Backend: Use existing metrics aggregator endpoints; add small projection for aggregated cost by model/route (7d/30d) to avoid full ETL changes
Tracing: Reuse runtime's existing trace emitter; add sampling config in control plane and store sampled traces in short-term indexed store (7d TTL)
Performance: Ensure dashboard widget queries use pre-aggregated timeseries at 1m resolution for default range to meet load targets
SLA: Put guardrails to throttle queries from Console to avoid cascading load on serving runtime during global incidents
